landscape._note: level_path is declared so apply_lighting.py's LEVEL GATE names THIS level. The gate exists because lighting was once written to the wrong world; it is satisfied here, not bypassed.
landscape._geometry_note: THERE IS NO LANDSCAPE HERE - the ground is a 300 m /Engine/BasicShapes/Plane at z=0. location_cm and z_scale_cm are read by apply_lighting.py:511-513 for one purpose only, parking the lighting actors somewhere findable in the viewport, and its own comment records that the value 'is not sampled by anything'. 5000 cm gives a 50 m span over trees measuring up to 16.95 m, so the sun parks at 37.5 m. These are NOT terrain geometry and nothing should read them as such.

_lighting_note: The R13 lighting VALUES are declared exactly once, in alpine_8k.json, and borrowed. Copying them here would be the duplicated-physical-description defect (NN24). This recipe declares only what genuinely differs: its own level.
_comment: SCRATCH LOOK-TEST SCENE for PN_interactiveSpruceForest (D2 intake). A flat plane and a size-spread of the pack's trees. It exists to answer two questions no property read can: does the wind ANIMATE without PN_GlobalUpdater (which would break every future frame A/B against this project's 0.00298 noise floor), and does the canopy read as a forest. It is NOT a biome recipe and declares no lighting of its own -- apply_lighting.py is run against recipes/alpine_8k.json so the R13 block stays declared in exactly one place (NN24). Delete the level freely; nothing references it.

capture._cameras_note: Two stations, both looking down +X (yaw 0) at trees standing on the x=0 line. rotation_deg is [pitch, yaw, roll], matching every camera in alpine_8k.json. `canopy_close` is the WIND instrument: wind displaces needles and branch tips, so a tight canopy framing is where an animating material shows up furthest above the 0.00298 noise floor. A wide station would dilute the same motion across mostly-empty sky and ground, which is the misleading-denominator trap (NN22).

cameras.name: spread_wide
cameras._what: Three trees across the size range at 35 m: small_06 (6.35 m), full_01 (10.52 m), half_01 (16.72 m). Judges whether the pack reads as a forest rather than as scrub.

cameras.name: canopy_close
cameras._what: spruce_half_01's canopy at 12 m, looking up. The wind A/B station.

ground._note: Plane is 100x100 cm, so scale 300 gives a 300 m square.

scratch._spacing_note: Tallest measured 16.95 m (spruce_half_01_low). 16 m spacing keeps crowns clear so each silhouette is judged alone. Wider than the PVE scratch scene's 14 m because these trees are taller.
scratch._trees_note: A size spread across the pack rather than every mesh: one sapling, one mid, one full and two of the tallest half forms. All 21 were MEASURED (Free/_measured/pn_spruce_forest.json); this scene is for the questions that need pixels. spruce_half_03 is included because it carries the pack's worst pivot offset, 0.293 m.
